Change the system configuration and watch the skeleton colour and state pages: the library implements onConfigurationChanged, so an instance whose colour and corner radius all derive from resources re-resolves in place without recreating the Activity.

Note: onConfigurationChanged only refreshes instances whose maskColor / highlightColor / cornerRadius were not explicitly overridden by XML, Theme or a global default — those re-read ssl_mask_default and friends under the new Configuration and clear the cached EMPTY / ERROR / LOADING state pages so they re-inflate on next display; any instance with an explicit override keeps the host brand colour. The skeleton template is re-inflated by the renderer on its own, keyed on configuration.hashCode(). This sample installs a global maskColor and cornerRadius, so the instance on this page is not resource-derived: it keeps the brand colour across a day/night switch, while its state pages and template are still rebuilt under the new Configuration. To exercise the resource-derived path, leave all three fields undeclared in both the global default and the XML. The "Recreate Activity" button is there for contrast: after a full recreation everything is resolved from scratch under the new Configuration.

Retry taps: %1$d (the unified retry entry the library wires up for you)

Note: the three IDs inside the built-in layouts are a public contract — ssl_builtin_state_root / ssl_builtin_state_message / ssl_builtin_state_retry. When ssl_errorRetryViewId is not set explicitly, the widget binds the built-in retry button as the unified retry entry automatically. To change the copy or swap in your own widget, call getStateView(ERROR) for the root node and replace it via findViewById; the built-in layouts only use android:* attributes so the fallback pages pull in neither Material nor AppCompat.
One skeleton instance covers the whole screen of rows, and the list Adapter is never replaced

Why a full-screen template instead of one instance per item: every instance builds its own full-size ALPHA_8 mask, so eight rows means eight per-pixel mask buffers growing linearly with the row count; each instance also subscribes to the animation clock — the library now shares one ticker across instances, but the mask memory is still one buffer per instance. This page reaches the same visual result with a single instance plus a static eight-row template, so memory is independent of how long the list is.
